title: UMass Defeats Rutgers 37-21, Snaps 16-Game Losing Streak to FBS Opponents
dek: UMass defeated Rutgers 37-21 on Friday, September 4, snapping a 16-game losing streak against FBS opponents while entering as 29.5-point underdogs. The Minutemen, who went 0-12 last season, delivered the largest upset loss for Rutgers since the FBS-FCS split in 1978.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: UMass scored on each of its first four drives and did not punt until 100 seconds remained in the third quarter, while Rutgers was held scoreless in the second and third quarters and committed four turnovers without forcing any.
bottom_line: Rutgers' next game against Boston College will determine whether Schiano's job becomes immediately at risk or whether the program can steady itself. The Minutemen, now 1-0, travel to face Kansas next, their second consecutive game against a team from the Power Four.
body:
UMass defeated Rutgers 37-21 on Friday, September 4, in a Week 1 upset that snapped a 16-game losing streak against FBS opponents while the Minutemen entered the game as 29.5-point underdogs, per CBS Sports and Sporting News reporting.
The victory marked UMass's first win against an FBS program since October 28, 2023, when the team defeated Army 21-14. The Minutemen went 0-12 last season and had never beaten a Power Four team since moving to the FBS level in 2012. By margin of defeat, the result was Rutgers's largest upset loss since the FBS and FCS split in 1978, making it the biggest upset by any FBS team since Kansas defeated Texas as a 31-point underdog in 2021.
UMass quarterback  Watson spent the last three seasons at Virginia Tech before transferring to UMass in the offseason; he was a three-star recruit and the No. 44 quarterback in the 2023 signing class. UMass scored on each of its first four drives and did not punt until there were 100 seconds remaining in the third quarter. The Minutemen built a 24-7 halftime lead and held Rutgers scoreless in the second and third quarters.
The defensive performance contradicted UMass's 2025 season statistics: the team allowed 38.6 points per game last season, ranking 136th nationally, and 433.8 total yards per game, ranking 129th. Against Rutgers, UMass generated seven tackles for loss and five sacks while winning the turnover battle 4-0 with three interceptions of Scarlet Knights quarterback Dylan Lonergan. According to Sporting News, Rutgers allowed no push up front on run defense and surrendered just 30 rushing yards while averaging 1.2 yards per carry. UMass rushed for 200 yards in the game. UMass forced a turnover on downs on a Rutgers 4th-and-1 attempt from the UMass 11-yard line with just under four minutes left in the third quarter, per CBS Sports.
Rutgers, coached by Greg Schiano in his seventh season of his second tour at the university, had won six consecutive season openers before the loss. Between his two stints, Schiano is the winningest coach in Rutgers history with 99 wins. Rutgers had consecutive bowl records for the first time since joining the Big Ten before missing the postseason this past season. The team's defense ranked last in the Big Ten in 2025. Rutgers faces significant financial and organizational challenges: the program reported a $78 million financial deficit in 2025 and is in the red more than $500 million since joining the Big Ten, per CBS Sports. Rutgers ranks as the lowest team in the Power Four in donor contributions, comparable to William & Mary and Wichita State. In 2025, the program reported just $2.7 million in sponsorship and licensing. Rutgers hired Kelli Zinn as athletic director, drawing her from a high-ranking position at LSU.
Rutgers's schedule includes a road trip to Boston College and faces difficult matchups ahead in conference play. A postgame fireworks display that had been scheduled in advance regardless of the result created an awkward optics moment, though sources note the show was not a reaction to the loss.
